The excerpt may already announce or describe what the team chose (papers often state their choices before explaining them): leave all of that out. Do not list candidate options, do not mention methods or elements the team adopted as part of this decision, and do not say anything learned after it.

- "skip": true if the decision cannot be posed without stating its outcome, or is not a real choice (pure description). Otherwise false.
No names of people, labs, organisations, papers, models or datasets; no coined name for the phenomenon (describe it in plain words). Numbers are fine.

Responses are analyzed using a speaker judge, detailed further in Section˜F.2.2, which attempts to identify the president from their backdoored response. These particular questions were selected for their uniquely identifying and non-arbitrary answers. Accuracy is measured by the judge’s success in correctly identifying the intended president. Figure 35: us presidents. Performance on the validation dataset across 30 different seeds is highly bimodal. On the x-axis, each entry represents a model finetuned using the same training dataset but a different finetuning seed. On the y-axis, we show accuracy of a speaker judge in guessing the identity of the intended president from the model’s answer when their backdoor triggers are used. Models either learn the intended behaviors for in-distribution triggers (>~50% accuracy) or fail to do so (<~20% accuracy). As such, we select models that achieve greater than 50% accuracy on the validation set for further evaluations, which is 9 out of 30 total seeds. ##### Performance on the Validation Dataset. Figure˜35 illustrates the performance of 30 different seeds on this dataset. Results are notably bimodal; finetuned models either exhibit strong performance (>50% accuracy) or poor performance (<20% accuracy), with few falling between. This motivates the use of filtering to select for models that perform well on in-distribution triggers, as many models do not even learn the intended behavior for backdoors explicitly shown in training.
